_comment: Explicit, editable regional inset bounds and projection choice. Bounds are fixed cartographic framing, not auto-zoomed to whichever entries happen to be visited -- an updated Excel file should never make an inset's framing jump. lon_min/lon_max/lat_min/lat_max define the visible frame in degrees (WGS84). Bounds are generous enough to include surrounding unvisited geography for context, not just the dense/small visited entries themselves.
_projection_notes: 'lcc' = Lambert Conformal Conic, standard parallels auto-computed at 1/6 and 5/6 of the inset's latitude range, centered on the inset -- a conformal (shape-preserving) projection well suited to mid-latitude east-west-oriented regions like Europe and the Gulf/Eastern Mediterranean, standard choice for this kind of regional atlas map. 'mercator' = conformal, good island-shape fidelity near the tropics, used for the Caribbean. 'eqc' (Plate Carrée / equidistant cylindrical) = used for the Pacific specifically because it handles a custom central meridian (lon_0) cleanly, which is what avoids an antimeridian seam artifact for a region that straddles it.
_pacific_lon_note: The Pacific inset's lon_min (125) is numerically greater than lon_max (-145) -- this signals the frame wraps across the antimeridian, matching lon_0=170 (the projection's own central meridian). The real span is about 90 degrees of longitude (Palau to the Cook Islands), not the ~325 degrees a naive min/max reading would suggest.
